name: Miter
overview: The miter, as described in Exodus 28 and 39, is a sacred garment made of fine linen that the Lord commanded to be worn by Aaron and his sons in their priestly duties. It was designed to accompany other holy vestments, signifying the consecration and sanctity required for ministering before God. A gold plate engraved with 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' was affixed to the forefront of the miter, symbolizing the priest's role in bearing the iniquity of the holy things and ensuring the offerings of Israel were accepted by God. This garment underscores the holiness and responsibility entrusted to the priesthood in their service to the Lord.
